more.title: Synthetic molecules self-assemble into triple helices with new control method
more.summary: Researchers at the University of Jyväskylä, Finland, have developed a new strategy for programming synthetic molecules to self-assemble into precisely defined three-dimensional structures. The study brings scientists a step closer to achieving the sophisticated molecular organization found in nature and could eventually open new possibilities for the development of advanced functional materials.

more.title: Beehives act as 'living immune systems' with layered antimicrobial defenses
more.summary: Researchers have discovered honey beehives act as "living immune systems" that help protect the bee colony, its offspring and food supplies from disease. The finding underlines the need to protect bee habitat to ensure their health.

more.title: Planting trees is not enough: Lasting climate benefits depend on land rights and livelihoods
more.summary: A new LMU study shows that three-quarters of the estimated global potential for new forests to capture CO₂ is threatened by significant social and institutional challenges.

more.title: Expanded earned income tax credit improved housing security for childless young adults
more.summary: A temporary expansion to the earned income tax credit improved housing security for young workers who don't have children, a new study shows.

more.title: New 4D biofabrication technology holds promise for tissue engineering, wound healing
more.summary: If you've ever created a snowflake by folding, cutting and unfolding a piece of paper, you've practiced the art of kirigami. Like origami, kirigami has inspired innovations far beyond the elementary school classroom, with applications ranging from deployable structures for spacecraft to semiconductors.

more.title: How enzymes locally block cell wall repair, allowing cells to fuse in an irreversible manner
more.summary: The fusion of two cells is a decisive event in the sexual reproduction of many organisms. In fungi, cells must not only bring their membranes together and merge them, but also locally open their protective cell wall.

more.title: Batteries help reduce emissions, but how do we reduce their emissions?
more.author: Scott K. Johnson
more.summary: One way to make batteries cleaner is to make fewer of them.

more.title: AI Proved the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis. What Happens Now?
more.author: Konstantin Kakaes
more.summary: Unlike other recent AI proofs, this one has been unpacked by human experts. The implications, one mathematician said, are “staggering.” The post AI Proved the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis. What Happens Now? first appeared on Quanta Magazine

more.title: Russian spacecraft maneuvers in "extreme proximity" to satellite used by Ukraine
more.author: Stephen Clark
more.summary: "Kosmos 2612 closed from hundreds of kilometers away to extreme proximity to ICEYE-X36."

more.title: Synthetic public opinion polling: AI personas don't always change their minds like real voters do
more.summary: A voter surveyed in October may give a different answer by January. An AI persona might not, depending on how it's built.

more.title: NZ's climate in 'uncharted territory,' with more extreme weather events ahead
more.summary: Much is being made of a record-strength El Niño event that could well spell a drier, windier summer for the north and east of New Zealand. But, as a major new assessment shows, it is forming against a backdrop of warming that's pushed the country's climate into "uncharted territory."

more.title: Khosla Ventures doubles down on Even Healthcare to challenge India’s hospital economics
more.author: Jagmeet Singh
more.summary: Even Healthcare reaches a $300 million valuation in a Khosla Ventures-led round as it plans to expand its hospital network in India.

more.title: Juvenile striped bass maintaining average abundance in Virginia waters in 2026
more.summary: Preliminary results from an ongoing long-term survey conducted by William & Mary's Virginia Institute of Marine Science (VIMS) suggest that an average year class of young-of-year striped bass was produced in the Virginia tributaries of the Chesapeake Bay in 2026. Striped bass are an important top predator in the Chesapeake Bay ecosystem and a valuable resource for commercial and recreational anglers.

more.title: Q&A: How does technology help track foodborne pathogens and outbreaks?
more.summary: After a cyclospora outbreak and recalls of imported beef over the summer, a recent Gallup poll found that Americans' confidence in food safety has fallen to a record low, and consumers may be wondering how foodborne illness outbreaks can be tracked and mitigated.

more.title: Alaska’s monster tsunami sent water 1,580 feet up a mountain
more.summary: A massive landslide in Alaska triggered the second-highest tsunami ever recorded, sending water and debris 1,580 feet up a mountainside just hours after tourists visited the area. Scientists discovered that the disaster was preceded by several warning signs, including rapid glacier retreat, heavy rainfall, and thousands of tiny seismic tremors.

more.title: Why some people escape Alzheimer’s despite carrying a high-risk gene
more.summary: Scientists have discovered why some people with a high genetic risk of Alzheimer’s remain mentally sharp into their 80s, uncovering a rare mutation that protects the brain from harmful protein buildup. The findings reveal a potential new way to prevent early brain damage and could pave the way for treatments that mimic this natural defense.

more.title: Something strange is happening beneath a volcano near 2 million people
more.summary: Scientists have discovered evidence of two hidden magma sources beneath Nicaragua’s Masaya volcano, where satellite observations revealed mysterious ground movements suggesting magma is shifting deep underground. The findings could improve eruption forecasting for the active volcano, which sits near 2 million people and attracts tourists to its spectacular lava lake.

more.title: Students take up to 88 standardized tests before high school, but more testing doesn't improve learning
more.summary: The public K-12 school system in the United States has become pervasively shaped by standardized testing.

more.title: Just 3,000 steps a day may help slow Alzheimer's, scientists find
more.summary: Walking just 3,000 steps a day could help slow Alzheimer’s-related brain changes, according to new research. Scientists discovered that physical activity was linked to less buildup of harmful tau proteins and nearly half the cognitive and functional decline, even in people already showing early signs of the disease.

more.title: A simple touch can bring dying corals back to life in just 7 weeks
more.summary: Scientists have discovered that severely bleached corals can make a remarkable comeback simply by touching healthy, genetically identical corals. In laboratory experiments, dying corals regained their color and fully recovered within seven weeks, with as little as five days of contact sometimes enough to start the healing process.
